newsitem.title: UK: Plastic packaging on rise in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Plastic packaging on rise in Asia.

text.p: The use of plastic packaging is on the rise in Asia, spurred by a growing trend toward instant and frozen foods, a market analyst firm reported on Tuesday.

Plastic packaging, including laminated bags and vacuum food packaging, is becoming increasingly common in Asian countries with developed networks of supermarkets and convenience stores, Euromonitor said in its report the Market for Packaged Food in South East Asia.

The growing similarity between southeast Asian and western eating and food shopping habits is expected to lead to strong growth in the use of packaging materials used in frozen foods convenience foods, Euromonitor said.

Plastic is the dominant packaging material in the Philippines, with a 45 percent market share. In Singapore and in Taiwan laminate has increased its market share to eight percent each over the last five years. In Thailand increased sales of dairy products such as milk and yoghurt have driven the demand for laminated containers, Euromonitor said.
But in other countries, traditional packaging materials continue to dominate.
Tin cans dominate in Malaysia with 35 percent of the market, while in Hong Kong paper and cardboard are the most popular material with a 47.5 percent market shares, Euromonitor said.

Glass is being used increasingly in Singapore and other southeast Asian countries to replace both polyvinyl chloride and paper containers due to growing environmental concerns of consumers and their aesthetic appeal, Euromonitor said.
